source: GSC > Indexing > Pages > Export (the API does not expose coverage; this is a hand export)
note: Baseline for judging the publish throttle (data/publish-throttle.json) on 2026-09-10. The series is a step function because GSC refreshes coverage every few days, not daily.

slopePerDay.reading: Every page made since 07-25 landed in the not-indexed pile, and the indexed count did not move once in a month. New-page indexation was effectively 0%.

verdict.why: notIndexed falling is ambiguous - Google may simply have dropped the pages. The only unambiguous win is the indexed count leaving the 5,232 plateau it has sat on since 07-25.

thresholds.win: indexed > 5300 - indexation restarted; keep the throttle and raise intake slowly, re-measuring each step
thresholds.drainingButNotIndexing: notIndexed < 7993 while indexed stays flat - Google is clearing the queue without keeping the pages; the pages themselves are the problem, not the queue
thresholds.intakeWasNotTheConstraint: notIndexed near 8343 (7993 + 14 days x 25/day) with indexed flat - our intake fell as designed but Google absorbed nothing, so crawl budget is purely an authority problem and backlinks are the only lever left; restore publish-throttle.json
thresholds.throttleNotApplied: notIndexed above 10000 - that is the old ~162/day slope continuing; check that the throttle actually took effect before drawing any conclusion
